A MOMENT FOR YOUR MIND

How to do a self-reflection check-in

Set aside a few minutes, pick an everyday moment, and write down what you remember about it.

1. Pick one specific moment

Choose a moment you can describe in a sentence. You might pick a conversation that stayed on your mind, a decision you kept putting off, or an ordinary moment that went well.

Try: “On Tuesday I left a group chat after a message landed badly.” You can look at that one moment without trying to sum up your whole week.

2. Write what you noticed

Write what happened, what you felt, and what you did next. Keep each part short. For example: “They asked why I hadn’t replied. I felt put on the spot. I closed the chat and came back an hour later.”

If an assumption comes up, write it alongside the details you know. “I thought they were upset with me” and “They asked why I hadn’t replied” describe different parts of the same moment.

3. Choose one step to try

Pick something small enough to use in a similar situation. You could tell someone you need a moment to think, ask what they meant, or repeat something that already helped. Write it in your own words and revisit it when useful.
